title: Write a QA Report Another Person Can Act On
subtitle: State the observed behavior, reproduction context, evidence, and acceptance check.
description: Turn a vague defect report into a compact handoff that distinguishes what was observed from what is suspected and gives the receiver enough context to reproduce, investigate, and verify the fix.

lifeOsSource.hack: A useful QA handoff separates observation from hypothesis and gives the receiver enough context to reproduce the issue and verify the expected result.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Write a one-line observed problem and context, add the smallest reliable reproduction sequence, attach the relevant evidence while removing secrets and personal data, label any suspected cause as a hypothesis, state the expected behavior, and define a narrow acceptance check for the fix.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Can another person see what happened, reproduce or investigate it, distinguish fact from hypothesis, and know what would count as fixed?

faq.question: Should every bug report include a suspected cause?
faq.answer: No. Add a hypothesis only when you have a useful reason for it, and label it clearly. A precise observation with reproducible context is better than a confident guess.
faq.answerHtml: No. Add a hypothesis only when you have a useful reason for it, and label it clearly. A precise observation with reproducible context is better than a confident guess.

faq.question: How much log or trace data should I attach?
faq.answer: Include enough to identify the failing behavior and relevant context without burying the report. Remove credentials, tokens, personal data, and unrelated payloads before sharing diagnostic material.
faq.answerHtml: Include enough to identify the failing behavior and relevant context without burying the report. Remove credentials, tokens, personal data, and unrelated payloads before sharing diagnostic material.

intro.html: A defect report is a handoff. Its job is to make the next investigation cheaper and safer, not to prove that the reporter already knows the cause. A compact report keeps observations, reproduction context, hypotheses, and acceptance criteria distinct.

sections.title: 1. Start with the observable problem
sections.html: Write one sentence describing what happened and where: feature, environment, relevant state, and visible failure. Avoid blame and avoid explaining the cause before the behavior itself is clear.

sections.title: 2. Add the smallest reliable reproduction context
sections.html: List the prerequisites, inputs, and sequence needed to encounter the problem. Include version, platform, account state, feature flag, or sample data only when it matters. Say when the issue is intermittent rather than presenting one occurrence as a deterministic sequence.

sections.title: 3. Attach focused diagnostic material
sections.html: Add the screenshot, request identifier, trace excerpt, console output, or other artifact that helps locate the failure. Remove secrets and unrelated personal data. Put suspected causes in a separately labeled hypothesis so the receiver can challenge them without disputing the observation.

sections.title: 4. State expected behavior and the acceptance check
sections.html: Describe what should happen instead and the narrow condition that would demonstrate the fix in the reported context. If broader regression coverage is needed, keep that as a separate verification task rather than expanding the original defect indefinitely.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace fabricated engineering-org results, unsupported cycle-time reductions, pseudo-optimal evidence quantities, invented social effects, and over-specific universal QA prescriptions with a practical defect-reporting template.
